content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese is a fresh cheese curd product obtained by curdling milk and draining the whey. It has a mild, slightly tangy flavor and a creamy, lumpy texture. Cottage cheese is eaten on its own, used in cooking, baking, and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is one of the oldest dairy foods, with evidence of its consumption in ancient Egypt.
It is known by different names worldwide: "cottage cheese" in the US, "tvorog" in Russia, and "fromage blanc" in France.
Cottage cheese comes in various fat levels, from non‑fat to about 9‑10 % milk fat.
There are "small curd" (soft) and "large curd" (firm) varieties, differing by the size of the curd grains.
It is often used as a base for cheese fillings, dumplings, and classic cottage cheese pancakes (syrniki).

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Cottage cheese provides high‑quality dairy protein that supports muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Calcium in cottage cheese helps maintain strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Its low sugar content makes it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: It supplies vitamin B12, riboflavin, and niacin, which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic potential
items.content: Live cultures in some cottage cheese varieties may support a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance may experience discomfort after consuming cottage cheese, especially low‑fat versions with higher lactose content.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey proteins can cause reactions to cottage cheese.

items.title: Added sodium in some products
items.content: Certain pre‑packaged cottage cheese varieties contain added salt, which may be a concern for those with hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cottage cheese can be enjoyed as a snack, mixed into smoothies, oatmeal, salads, used as a filling for pancakes, dumplings, or baked into casseroles and cheese pancakes. Sweet versions are often combined with fruit, honey, or jam.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cottage cheese in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in a sealed container. It typically remains fresh for 5‑7 days after opening. Discard if it develops a sour odor, mold, or an off‑texture.
